The season began on 3 February and ended on 2 December 2023. Thirty-seven teams competed in the league, thirty-three of which took part in the [[2022 Primera Nacional|2022 season]], along with two teams relegated from [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División]], one team promoted from [[Torneo Federal A]] and another one promoted from [[Primera B Metropolitana]]. [[Independiente Rivadavia]] promoted to Primera División and won the competition for the first time in this season, defeating [[Club Almirante Brown|Almirante Brown]] 2–0 after extra time in the championship final played on 29 October 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.elgrafico.com.ar/articulo/futbol-de-ascenso/70729/independiente-rivadavia-ascendio-a-primera-division-y-se-consagro-campeon |title=Independiente Rivadavia se consagró campeón y ascendió a Primera División |trans-title=Independiente Rivadavia crowned themselves as champions and promoted to Primera División |publisher=[[El Gráfico (Argentina)|El Gráfico]] |language=es |date=29 October 2023 |access-date=30 October 2023}} The other promoted side was [[Deportivo Riestra]], who won the Torneo Reducido after defeating [[Deportivo Maipú]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.infobae.com/deportes/2023/12/02/deportivo-maipu-y-deportivo-riestra-definen-el-ultimo-boleto-a-primera-en-la-final-del-reducido-de-la-primera-nacional-hora-tv-y-formaciones/ |title=Riestra ascendió tras vencer 1-0 a Deportivo Maipú y jugará en la Liga Profesional por primera vez en su historia |trans-title=Riestra promoted after beating Deportivo Maipú 1–0 and will play in the Liga Profesional for the first time in history |publisher=[[Infobae]] |language=es |date=2 December 2023 |access-date=2 December 2023}} ==Format== For this season, the competition was played under a format similar to the one used for the [[2021 Primera Nacional|2021 season]], with the thirty-seven participating teams being split into two zones, one of 19 teams and another one of 18 teams, where they played against the other teams in their group twice: once at home and once away, with one team in Zone A having a bye in each round. No interzonal or derby matchdays were played, and teams from the same city were drawn into different zones. Both zone winners played a final match on neutral ground to decide the first promoted team to the [[Argentine Primera División|Liga Profesional]] for the 2024 season, while the teams placed from second to eighth place in each zone played a knockout tournament (''Torneo Reducido'') for the second promotion berth along with the loser of the final between the zone winners, which joined the Reducido in the second round. The teams placing in bottom place of each zone were relegated at the end of the season, with a third relegated team slated to be decided in a playoff match between the sides placing second-from-bottom in each group.{{cite web|url=https://www.tycsports.com/primera-nacional/como-se-juega-la-primera-nacional-2023-el-nuevo-formato-con-37-equipos-dos-grupos-y-mas-cambios-id484469.html |title=Cómo se juega la Primera Nacional 2023: el nuevo formato con 37 equipos, dos grupos y más cambios |trans-title=How is the 2023 Primera Nacional played: the new format with 37 teams, two groups and more changes |publisher=[[TyC Sports]] |language=es |date=28 December 2022 |access-date=29 December 2022}} However, the third relegation from Primera Nacional and consequently, the relegation playoffs, were cancelled by the [[Argentine Football Association]] on 23 October 2023 in order to have a 38-team competition for [[2024 Primera Nacional|2024]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ole.com.ar/futbol-ascenso/primera-nacional-promocion-tercer-descenso_0_kE4R7aN3e2.html |title=Insólito: se anuló el tercer descenso de la Primera Nacional |trans-title=Unbelievable: the Primera Nacional's third relegation was voided |publisher=[[Olé (sports newspaper)|Olé]] |language=es |date=23 October 2023 |access-date=24 October 2023}} This
